description: Circular ring buffer overwriting old items on overflow fails to advance tail read pointer, corrupting FIFO read order.
spec_notes: CircularBuffer.write must advance tail when count == capacity to maintain correct unread queue head.

"""Fixed-capacity ring buffer with overwrite policy."""

from typing import Any, List, Optional


class CircularBuffer:
    def __init__(self, capacity: int = 5):
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.buf: List[Optional[Any]] = [None] * capacity
        self.head = 0  # Write pointer
        self.tail = 0  # Read pointer
        self.count = 0

    def write(self, item: Any) -> Optional[Any]:
        overwritten = None
        if self.count == self.capacity:
            overwritten = self.buf[self.head]
            self.buf[self.head] = item
            self.head = (self.head + 1) % self.capacity
            # BUG: When buffer is full and overwrites, tail pointer must also advance
            # to maintain valid FIFO order! Fails to update tail pointer.
        else:
            self.buf[self.head] = item
            self.head = (self.head + 1) % self.capacity
            self.count += 1
        return overwritten

    def read(self) -> Optional[Any]:
        if self.count == 0:
            return None
        val = self.buf[self.tail]
        self.buf[self.tail] = None
        self.tail = (self.tail + 1) % self.capacity
        self.count -= 1
        return val

    def is_full(self) -> bool:
        return self.count == self.capacity

from ring_stream import RingStreamLogger
from consumer import StreamConsumer


def test_basic_fifo_drain():
    logger = RingStreamLogger(capacity=3)
    logger.log_event("e1")
    logger.log_event("e2")
    consumer = StreamConsumer(logger)
    assert consumer.consume_latest_batch() == ["e1", "e2"]
    assert consumer.consume_latest_batch() == []


def test_overwrite_on_overflow_preserves_most_recent_items():
    logger = RingStreamLogger(capacity=3)
    # Write 5 events into capacity 3 buffer: e1, e2, e3, e4, e5
    # e1 and e2 are overwritten. Buffer must contain [e3, e4, e5] in order!
    for ev in ["e1", "e2", "e3", "e4", "e5"]:
        logger.log_event(ev)
    consumer = StreamConsumer(logger)
    assert consumer.consume_latest_batch() == ["e3", "e4", "e5"]


def test_repeated_wraparound_continuous_streaming():
    logger = RingStreamLogger(capacity=2)
    logger.log_event("a")
    logger.log_event("b")
    logger.log_event("c")  # Overwrites "a", tail points to "b"
    consumer = StreamConsumer(logger)
    assert consumer.consume_latest_batch() == ["b", "c"]
    # Write again after drain
    logger.log_event("d")
    assert consumer.consume_latest_batch() == ["d"]


def test_empty_buffer_drain():
    logger = RingStreamLogger(capacity=5)
    consumer = StreamConsumer(logger)
    assert consumer.consume_latest_batch() == []


def test_interleaved_write_and_reads():
    logger = RingStreamLogger(capacity=2)
    logger.log_event("1")
    assert logger.buffer.read() == "1"
    logger.log_event("2")
    logger.log_event("3")
    logger.log_event("4")  # Overwrites 2
    assert logger.drain_all() == ["3", "4"]


def test_is_full_predicate():
    logger = RingStreamLogger(capacity=2)
    assert logger.buffer.is_full() is False
    logger.log_event("x")
    assert logger.buffer.is_full() is False
    logger.log_event("y")
    assert logger.buffer.is_full() is True
